_doc: M20 exit-refinement coverage matrix — one row per strategy leg. THE milestone's done-condition: every live leg carries a verdict per lever column (shipped / honest_negative / pending / blocked:<reason>). Update in the SAME PR as any verdict-producing work (binding per .claude/skills/exit-refinement). Statuses only from verified evidence (memo/sprint-log/PR refs) — never inferred. ROWS ARE ONE LEG EACH as of 2026-08-09 (BL-20260809-COVERAGE-MATRIX-MULTILEG-ROW-ONE-STATUS): bundled rows carried ONE status for a whole family, so the status described only the leg that passed and the roll-up over-counted `shipped`. Exploded rows carry `exploded_from`. The `shadow fleet` row is deliberately NOT exploded — its label does not enumerate its legs and it is execution:shadow, outside the live-leg done-condition. DO NOT ADD A NEW BUNDLED ROW.

legend.honest_negative: tested, failed the gate — hard levers/trail stand
legend.shipped_gate_failed: LIVE in config, but a LATER re-sweep failed its gate and the operator chose to HOLD (ref = memo/date). Deliberately distinct from both neighbours: `honest_negative` implies NOT live (recording a live lever there is exactly the bug that made trend_donchian's trail_decay read as a closed negative), and `shipped` asserts 'validated + live' which overclaims once the validation no longer reproduces. A cell here carries a STANDING decision to keep a lever whose justification has lapsed, so it must stay visible in the done-condition roll-up rather than be absorbed into either bucket.

Expected value is LOW, on three grounds, only the first two of which are measured. (1) FLEET PRIOR IS NEGATIVE. vol_trail was swept fleet-wide on 2026-08-13 across 6 legs and returned exactly ONE candidate (qqq_pullback_1h, wf 6/6, passed_unshipped); one honest_negative (scha); four blocked for thin data. Partial-TP banking, which is what exit_ladder expresses, is the milestone-wide honest negative of memo section 7.2 (banking loses net_R across 45 rows). Neither prior is evidence about THIS leg — the matrix _doc forbids an inherited verdict and this note does not claim one — but a prior that weak is a poor reason to spend harness work. (2) THE SAMPLE MAY NOT SUPPORT A VERDICT EVEN IF THE LEVER EXISTED. Deepest recorded backtest depth for this leg is n=135 at a 2900d lookback (docs/research/RESEARCH-RIGOR-STANDARD.md line 94); at 730d it is n=28. A derived IS/OOS split of n=135 lands the OOS base in roughly the 25-35 band against the harness's 25-trade floor — i.e. MARGINAL, not comfortably clear. That is the same regime that returned blocked:insufficient_oos_base_at_derived_split for iwm/splg in the 2026-08-13 vol_trail sweep, so the plausible outcome of building the lever is another blocked cell rather than a verdict. Stated as a range because it is arithmetic on a recorded n, NOT a run: the actual split is resolve_split's to compute and it has surprised me before (probe error #8 — I screened eligibility off matrix lifetime refs and the harness measured materially lower). (3) The leg is BTC 4h, the slowest cadence in the fleet, so accrual will not relieve (2) on any near horizon. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS: a measured lifetime count for this leg above roughly 2x the OOS floor at the split the harness actually derives — measure it, do not project it — or a fleet vol_trail/banking result that stops being a coin flip.

vol_trail.ref: BLOCKED: insufficient OOS base. OOS n=4 at the corpus-standard split 2025-07-01 and n=12 at 2023-01-01, both under the floor of 25; leg lifetime is 33 trades. Measured twice, PR #8849: split 2025-07-01 (run 31655236776) and again at split 2023-01-01 (run 31655318804) to test whether the window, not the data, was binding. LIVE-PARITY geometry tp_cap_pct=0.099. Rows in docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl. Moving the split is NOT the fix: it lifted OOS n from 4 to 12, still short, while shrinking IS. Unblocks when either the leg accrues more OOS trades or the operator settles the evidence standard for low-frequency legs. WHY THIS IS NOT `honest_negative`: the cell terminated at `insufficient_base` — the OOS base is under MIN_OOS_TRADES=25 — which is 'we did not have enough trades to look', the opposite claim from 'we looked and the lever failed'. Recording it as a negative would be the same collapse BL-20260809-COVERAGE-MATRIX-MULTILEG-ROW-ONE-STATUS names. AND the walk-forward — the test whose folds span the FULL history and which this leg's lifetime CAN support — is skipped by that same branch (m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:1442-1451, `if _thin: ... elif candidate: walkforward(...)`), so the leg is refused the one test its data would sustain. See BL-20260813-THIN-OOS-BLOCKS-THE-WALKFORWARD-IT-COULD-PASS. || STATUS SUFFIX ADDED 2026-08-13 (no re-measurement — the ref already named the cause; only the status string was silent). This cell read a BARE `blocked`, the one cell in the matrix whose status did not carry its reason. That is a collapsed state by the repo's own rule: the roll-up normalises via `base()` (split on ':'), so a bare `blocked` is indistinguishable in the per-reason breakdown from a cell whose cause was never established — 'we know exactly why and it is a thin OOS base' and 'nobody recorded why' landed in the same bucket. Suffix chosen to match what was MEASURED, not what is likely: the sweep ran at EXPLICIT splits (2025-07-01, 2023-01-01) and terminated at insufficient_base with OOS n=4 and n=12 against MIN_OOS_TRADES=25, which is the same terminal state as the mes/mhg `giveback_stop` cells already carrying this suffix. DELIBERATELY NOT `insufficient_lifetime_trades`, even though that is probably where a re-run would land: lifetime 33 is under resolve_split's `2 x target` requirement (2 x 25 = 50), so a derived-split re-run would very likely fall back `leg_too_thin` exactly as spy (48) and qld (31) did in the 2026-08-13 re-sweep. But that is ARITHMETIC ON A RECORDED LIFETIME, NOT A RUN — the cell was measured under fixed splits before PR #8965's resolve_split existed, and stamping the projected reason would be recording a verdict the harness never returned. Consequence worth stating for whoever picks this up: re-running this cell under split-mode=oos-trades is NOT expected to unblock it, so it is a poor candidate for the next sweep. The headline is unmoved (`base()` maps both spellings to `blocked`); only the per-reason breakdown changes, 1 bare -> 0.

exit_head_ml.ref: E1 RE-RUN 2026-08-13 (relay #8963, fold-mode=trades, fold_blocks fix) — REASON CORRECTED, still blocked. 48 lifetime harness trades; a 50-trade test block needs >=100 for one fold, so BOTH fold modes yield 0. This is a sample-size limit, NOT the calendar-fold defect that blocked the pullback family (now graded). Unblocking needs more trades or a justified lower --min-fold-trades, not a re-run. Years-mode printed '16 candidate folds' here and produced nothing; trades-mode returns 0 and says so. || HORIZON MEASURED 2026-08-13: at 3.60 trades/yr (its 13 OOS trades over the 3.61y since split 2023-01-01 — a MEASURED rate, not a forecast), the 52 trades still needed arrive in about **14.5 YEARS**. `blocked:insufficient_lifetime_trades` reads as a hold that will clear; on this leg it will not clear on any planning horizon. Recorded as a fact on the cell WITHOUT changing its status — whether these become `n/a`, gain a distinct status, or the done-condition changes is a product decision about what M20 'done' means, and it is queued for the operator (BL-20260813-EXIT-HEAD-ML-1D-LEGS-UNREACHABLE). Caveat: the rate assumes the leg keeps trading as observed and stays live; a regime with more signals would shorten it. || ⚠️ THE HORIZON NOTE ABOVE IS WRONG AND IS RETRACTED (2026-08-13, operator challenge: "why aren't we using backtesting? nothing is ever supposed to need live soaking"). It framed the missing trades as arriving through FORWARD LIVE ACCRUAL. They do not. `lifetime harness trades` are produced by a BACKTEST over the built dataset, so the count is governed by HOW MUCH HISTORY WE BUILT, not by elapsed time. `scripts/ops/build_trainer_datasets.sh:925` sets `EQ_1D_START="${EQ_1D_START:-2015-01-01}"` and every equity 1d dataset is built from that date via yfinance — a CHOSEN window (~11.6y), not a limit of the available data. yfinance serves SPY from 1993, QQQ from 1999, IWM from 2000, SPLG from 2005, SCHA/TQQQ/QLD from 2009-2010. So this cell is blocked by a configuration default, and the remedy is a dataset rebuild over a longer window rather than a milestone decision or a wait. The arithmetic in the retracted note is still valid as a TRADES-PER-YEAR-OF-DATA rate — only the forward-in-time interpretation was wrong. NOT YET MEASURED: the actual span of the built files (trainer relay #9049 pending) and how many trades a longer window really yields, since the earlier-regime trade rate need not match the recent one. See BL-20260813-EXIT-HEAD-ML-1D-LEGS-UNREACHABLE. || ⚠️ SECOND CORRECTION, 2026-08-13, and it supersedes the EQ_1D_START note above on TWO points. (a) THE FILES DO NOT START AT 2015. Measured on the trainer (relay #9049): SPY_1d 2010-01-04..2026-07-07, 4152 rows. So EQ_1D_START's 2015-01-01 default is NOT what built these; field beats comment, and my '~11.6y chosen window' was wrong. (b) THE BAR IS 3x THE BLOCK, NOT 2x. `fold_blocks` yields u = floor(N/b) - 1 usable folds and `per_leg_summary` requires u >= 2, so a leg needs N >= 3b = **150** trades at block 50 — not the 100 this ref and every sibling states. At exactly 100 a leg gets ONE fold and the gate rejects it on `u >= 2`. CONSEQUENCE: extending to full inception does NOT rescue this leg — projecting the leg's own measured trades/yr over the extra history gives about 97 (from 1993) lifetime trades against the 150 needed, and ZERO of the seven equity legs reach it. So the data window is not the binding constraint after all; the BLOCK SIZE is, which is why it is being derived rather than assumed (operator decision 2026-08-13). Pending: relay #9055 measures the per-trade dispersion the derivation needs. Nothing here changes this cell's status. || ✅ BLOCK SIZE DERIVED 2026-08-13 — this cell's blocker is now understood and it is NOT an arbitrary number. docs/research/M20-E1-block-size-derivation-2026-08-13.md, measured over 21 e1_report.json / 262 folds / 15 groups: sigma_d ~0.747R, standardized effect delta ~0.105 (5 of 15 groups NEGATIVE). b=(z_p/delta)^2 puts the 0.75-0.80 per-fold reliability band at 41-64 trades and b=50 gives 0.771 — so 50 STAYS. Crucially the derivation also closes the route this cell invites: modelling the whole gate (>=2/3 of u folds, u=floor(N/b)-1) shows P_detect is NOT monotonic in b, and every apparent optimum sits at a u where 2/3 is cheap to hit by luck (50% single-condition false-positive rate), so tuning b to unblock legs would select the settings easiest to pass BY CHANCE. AT THIS LEG'S LIFETIME NO BLOCK SIZE YIELDS A TRUSTWORTHY VERDICT — at N=98 the only gradeable options give either 0.49 power or a 50% FP rate. The honest disposition is therefore NOT 'wait for trades' and NOT 'lower the block'; it is that the exit head's edge (delta ~0.105, inconsistent across families) is too small to grade on a leg this size. That upstream question is the open one.
